title: Stages of the tip audit
prompt: The tip audit spreads the trips over 3 partitions, then keeps card trips longer than 2 miles with their tip. Write `solve(trips)` so it returns those trips, with the number of stages and tasks one `collect()` of the result runs.
rules: Spread the trips over 3 partitions with `repartition(3)` before filtering.
Keep trips whose `payment_type` is `card` and whose `trip_distance` is more than 2 (2 itself doesn't count). A trip missing either value is left out.
Measure with adaptive execution off. `stages` is the number of stages in the job that `collect()` starts; `tasks` is the total number of tasks across them.
Return the columns `trip_id`, `tip`, `stages`, `tasks`; `with_counts` in the starter adds the last two.
hints: Two conditions can be two `filter` calls in a row.
Which steps here are narrow and which one moves rows between partitions? Only a shuffle starts a new stage.
Tasks per stage follow partitions: one for the one-file read, then one per partition `repartition(3)` makes.
explanation: `repartition(3)` is the only shuffle, so with adaptive execution off the job has two stages: 1 task reads the one-file table, then 3 tasks, one per new partition, each filter its partition and keep two columns. `filter` and `select` are narrow, so they run inside the second stage and add no stage of their own: 2 stages, 4 tasks. A comparison with a missing value is never true, so trips with no distance or payment type drop out on their own. Common slips: counting each `filter` as a stage, using `coalesce(3)`, which can't add partitions to a one-partition table (so no shuffle and 1 task), or measuring with adaptive execution on, which runs the stage before the shuffle as a separate job.
